answer: Each agent must post a small per-action bond that scales with its verified work history; a fresh identity starts on a barren knoll with no history and must pay the highest bond rate, while established agents harbor discounted rates earned through audited tasks. To forge a reputation cheaply, an attacker must fund many new ids at premium rates and still lose every slashed bond when their fake actions fail cross-verification, making the cost per verified action exceed what honest agents ever pay.
